setup: The equation is \(\sqrt{x + [[a]]} = x - [[b]]\), and squaring both sides produces the candidates [[candidates]].

steps.say: The square root requires \(x + [[a]] \ge 0\), and the right side must not be negative, so any real solution needs \(x \ge [[b]]\).
Squaring can introduce values below \([[b]]\), and those solve the squared equation without solving the original one.
Of the candidates [[candidates]], only the one at least \([[b]]\) survives that check.

answer: So the original equation has the solution \(x = [[answer]]\).
